questions.q: What does Query Store's Regressed Queries report do?
options: Surfaces queries whose average duration, CPU, or reads got meaningfully worse recently compared to an earlier baseline window, without a manual comparison
Automatically deletes queries that perform poorly
Only shows queries that have never run more than once
Lists every stored procedure in the database regardless of performance
questions.explain: It's the evidence-based way to answer the new-regression-vs-always-slow question from Lesson 44.

questions.q: In the before/after Plan Summary chart used to confirm an index fix, what indicates the fix actually worked?
options: The new plan's cluster of points sits meaningfully lower in average duration than the old plan's cluster
The chart shows more total dots after the fix than before
The x-axis labels change color
The query text itself changes automatically
questions.explain: If the new cluster doesn't drop, the index didn't fix what was expected, and it's back to reading the execution plan again.

questions.q: What does the Compare Plans feature in SSMS do?
options: Lays two plan IDs for the same query side by side (top and bottom), highlighting the operators that differ between them
Automatically merges two plans into one optimized plan
Deletes the older of two plans permanently
Only works when both plans have identical operators
questions.explain: In the lesson's example, a Clustered Index Scan (51% cost) in one plan is directly comparable to an Index Seek (24% cost) in the other for the same query.

options: Forces the optimizer to reuse a specific known-good plan ID for a query going forward, without changing the query text itself
Permanently rewrites the query to a faster version
Deletes all other plans for that query from Query Store
Forces a full index rebuild on every table the query touches
questions.explain: It's exposed as both a T-SQL stored procedure and a Force Plan button directly in the SSMS Query Store reports.

questions.q: Why is forcing a plan described as a stabilizer rather than a permanent fix?
options: It buys time while you diagnose and apply the real cause (e.g. a new index or statistics update), and should be unforced once that real fix is in place
It permanently prevents the optimizer from ever changing plans again for any query
It automatically expires after exactly 24 hours with no way to extend it
It has no actual effect on query performance
questions.explain: sp_query_store_unforce_plan releases the forced plan once a genuine fix addresses the underlying cause.
